To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the collective ground-state correlations are robust against variations of the SHFs, (ii) the collective GSC are large in the vicinity of the magic numbers and decrease with the distance from the magicity, (iii) the collective GCS are large in the region of the neutron drip line, (iv) collective GSC are larger for the neutron-rich nuclei compared to the neutron-deficient nuclei, (v) the collective GCM energies are in good agreement with the empirical data,
collective ground-state correlation energies are rather independent of nuclear bulk properties and that their magnitude is of the order of 1 MeV/nucleon.
collective ground-state correlation energies are rather robust under change of the Skyrne-Hartre-Fork functional and that they are of the order of a few percent of the total binding energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the microscopic description of collective ground-state correlations and their influence on the nuclear ground-state properties.
the systematic study of ground-state correlations in the nuclear many-body system.
the study of the microscopic origin and the systematic properties of collective ground-state correlations in nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
collective GSC are a robust feature of the nuclear mean field, independent of the particular choice of the SHF parameters.
collective GSCs are a universal property of nuclear matter, which is independent on the specific nuclear interaction.
the collective GSC are robust and universal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the collective GSC are a rather robust feature of the nuclear ground state and that they can be described in terms of a few collective degrees of freedom.
the GSCs are robust and can be reliably computed in the SHF model, thus providing a solid ground for the study of the collective properties of nuclei.
GSC are universal and can be described by a few simple scaling laws.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collective GSC are of similar magnitude as those of the pairing field.
collective ground-state correlation energies can be reliably predicted in the SHF model and are not a source of uncertainty in the description of nuclear properties.
the collective GSC are a robust and universal feature of nuclear structure.
